entry_state: The foreign subsidiary case preserves acquisition, profit, goodwill translation and owner-specific reserves through loss of control. Removing all subsidiary cash changes the group population, not the parent's legal cash payment. Full and retained-interest sales have equal equity but different cash; book identity and dated control bindings are now being specified.
exit_state: The group profile binds legal-book identities, currency units, control intervals and immutable branches. Group publication preserves legal books and exact retry identity; corrected source evidence creates a new view without overwriting the old explanation. The next section examines why an eliminated intragroup loan can leave a real currency exposure.
findings: The synthetic A/O/R/D calendar does not establish historical investor availability. Intermediate A/O worksheet states are not claimed as closed reports.
Full-sale and retained-interest proposals branch from one immutable reporting state rather than posting sequential alternatives.
A retry with its original fingerprint returns the prior receipt before treating its opening revision as stale; changed requests are not retries.
